reviews.title: Why. Just why.
reviews.text: In the past few months, the usability of the app has become questionable at best. Why does an ad have to pop in from the side and take up half the screen while I’m in the middle of watching a video? Why does that same side pop up ad like to appear as I’m trying to fast forward, forcing me to unintentionally click the ad? And after being forced to watch yet another ad every 5 minutes of a video, why does a pop up ad remain and take up 30% of the screen on the bottom left? Google and Alphabet have laid off many of their human employees in favor of AI bots, so surely it’s not about needing to make more revenue to be able to pay their employees fairly. So what is it? Ah, greed. The most blatant evidence of late-stage capitalism. You are actively worsening the consumer experience to make a few more cents off of every view. And now, to cap it all off, you remove the subscription feed? What kinda stupid, backwards, AI-driven move is that? How many times do the people have to tell you? WE DO NOT WANT AI FORCED INTO EVERYTHING. The main feed isn’t even suggesting videos I would like anymore. It is literally only giving me 20 shorts and videos from the past 5 creators I’ve watched. That’s it. I can reload the feed until I’m blue in the face, and I’m getting nothing remotely interesting. Half of the videos are ones I’ve already watched. So basically, how could you make a service beloved by billions become an absolute wasteland?

reviews.title: Your ‘Don’t Recommend’ Button Is Failing People
reviews.text:
I woke up at around 3am after a nightmare and couldn’t get back to sleep. I opened YouTube hoping to distract myself, calm down and bring myself back to earth. Instead, Shorts pushed me deeper and deeper into an algorithmic loop of distressing content, even while I was actively trying to tell it I did not want to see that kind of material.

I have OCD, and that night the algorithm contributed to one of the worst spikes I have ever experienced. It pushed me into a frightening mental state where I was having suicidal thoughts. That is how serious this became.

The “Don’t recommend” button needs far more weight. If I reject a type of content, showing me essentially the same thing from a different creator defeats the entire purpose. It is like giving someone a slice of cake, having them tell you they hate it, and then offering them another slice from the other side of the same cake. It is still the same cake.

YouTube does not know what the person on the other side of the screen is dealing with. They could be grieving, traumatised, mentally unwell, sleep-deprived, or already hanging by a thread. An algorithm that keeps feeding them upsetting content because it generates views and engagement can make a bad situation dramatically worse.

YouTube presents itself as a safe, welcoming platform, but the experience can feel completely different once Shorts locks onto the wrong theme. Removing meaningful dislike signals while leaving users with a weak “Don’t recommend” control feels deep

Been using this app for years now and it used to be good. Used to be able to watch a video, have it recommend some other good ones, and easily go through your subscription feed to find what’s been posted recently by those you follow. 

Now though? Let’s start with the most recent change. The subs area has been moved from being at the bottom of the app to being squeezed up at the top for no reason. It’s actively making it harder to find the content I like to follow. 

But the worst offender is the ads. Don’t get me wrong, I get and understand this content is being provided for free and the ads are needed to pay for stuff. I can accept that. What I don’t accept is how the ads load up crystal clear while the videos themselves don’t and look terrible. Or how most ads are becoming longer and longer and unskippable. Or how of you pause the screen shrinks and you get an ad in its place. Or how much of the ads are for extremely questionable products that are clearly AI slop or something that would be bad for your phone if you installed it, yet they make it super easy for you to click on it so it installs on your phone regardless when you’re just trying to close the ad.

There are many small problems that I’m starting to get fed up with. Most frustrating is that it keeps pushing videos by or about a particular creator I despised. I watched ONE video CRITICIZING this person, and now it’s constantly suggesting videos by them, reposting them and/or glazing them. Every time I click on Don’t Recommend Channel and yet they keep coming.
Secondly, it does not sync playback locations between the streamed and downloaded version of the same video. I mostly use the iPhone app for downloading videos and watching them on the subway. But I often want to switch to the streamed version when i am in cell range to look at the comments. It starts over every single time.
Thirdly, the recommended categories at the top of the app are different every time, and it seems like they purposely show categories that are different from what I clicked on last time. If I click on NBA, it doesn’t recommend NBA the next several times I use the app. Same with ASMR etc. Why can’t i just set the categories that are recommended? If i can, that functionality is way too hidden.
There’s at least one more thing I wanted to complain about, when I think of it I’ll come back and edit this.

reviews.title: Why there is no off switch to the Multi-Language Audio!!?
reviews.text:
Dear Johanna Voolich, I’m writing to express my absolute frustration with the current state of YouTube’s audio settings. Your product team has managed to create a feature that is both intrusive and impossible to disable globally.
Currently, the system is 'force-feeding' me dubbed content. If I change my interface language to stop the English videos from being dubbed in Chinese, the system then starts dubbing Chinese videos into English. Do your product managers understand the concept of a Bilingual User?
We are not all monolingual. Your team's failure to provide a simple 'Always Play Original Audio' toggle in the settings is a massive oversight in UX design. It’s patronizing and frankly, it makes the platform painful to use. Fix the logic or give us the switch."

reviews.title: Finally making the money they deserve
reviews.text:
They’ve added banners over videos after ads have played that require multiple taps to dismiss. There is not one human alive whose experience is improved by this change, unless their only contact with the platform is in their stock portfolios. It’s good, though; I’m happy knowing that every bit of joy I lose dismissing an ad I’ve already skipped is going to someone who really did something important with their life. Unfortunately, the fact that I, one of the swine, am being left any shred in which to find solace is an unforgivable mistake. Hopefully one day they’ll just chain my ankles behind my head and tattoo the ads the only place I can see them to give me the experience I really deserve.

Gave one star back for turning on sound for video previews every time I open the app. I turn it off because I think I know better than the developers, but they make sure to put me in my place by reminding me that it’s actually vitally important to hear every video I spend half a second looking at as I’m scrolling. Leaving them muted would give me the impression that I’m an agent with free will over my phone’s emissions. However, the very purpose of a telephone is to subject the owner to nonconsensual noises, so I am being given a valuable lesson every time my preferences are ignored.
